extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting manuscripts to Taylor & Francis journals (research article authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on composing a clear data availability (data access) statement that states where the research data are available and under what conditions, using publisher-approved templates and respecting journal policies and peer‑review anonymity. Includes templates for a range of situations (open data, restricted data, no new data, non-digital data, embargoes, third-party restrictions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: what a data availability statement is
rubrics_metrics.description: A data availability statement (also sometimes called a ‘data access statement’) tells the reader where the research data associated with a paper is available, and under what conditions the data can be accessed. They also include links (where applicable) to the data set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must state location and access conditions; include links/DOIs where applicable. This statement will be openly available on Taylor & Francis Online and may contribute to credit for research outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data openly available in a public repository that issues datasets with DOIs
rubrics_metrics.description: "The data that support the findings of this study are openly available in [repository name e.g “figshare”] at http://doi.org/[doi], reference number [reference number]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide repository name, DOI URL and reference number. Marked as usable under policy: All. Use exactly this style to make data findable and citable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data openly available in a public repository that does not issue DOIs
rubrics_metrics.description: "The data that support the findings of this study are openly available in [repository name] at [URL], reference number [reference number]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide repository name, direct URL and reference number. Marked as usable under policy: All. Ensure the URL is persistent where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data derived from public domain resources
rubrics_metrics.description: "The data that support the findings of this study are available in [repository name] at [URL/DOI], reference number [reference number]. These data were derived from the following resources available in the public domain: [list resources and URLs]"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the public domain sources and their URLs; provide repository/DOI and reference number. Policy: All. Make provenance clear by naming derived resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data available within the article or its supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: "The authors confirm that the data supporting the findings of this study are available within the article [and/or] its supplementary materials."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when all supporting data are included in the main article or supplementary files. Applicable for journals with Basic or Share upon Request policies as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data generated at a central, large-scale facility, available upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: "Raw data were generated at [facility name]. Derived data supporting the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author [initials] on request."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the facility where raw data were produced and clarify that derived data are available on request from the corresponding author. Marked for Basic and Share upon Request policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo on data due to commercial restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: "The data that support the findings will be available in [repository name] at [URL / DOI link] following a [6 month] embargo from the date of publication to allow for commercialization of research findings."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State repository, URL/DOI and explicit embargo duration and reason (e.g., commercialization). Use only where permitted by the journal’s data policy (Basic, Share upon Request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data available on request due to privacy/ethical restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: "The data that support the findings of this study are available on request from the corresponding author, [initials]. The data are not publicly available due to [restrictions e.g. their containing information that could compromise the privacy of research participants]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why data cannot be made public (privacy/ethical reasons) and give contact for requests. Use where participant privacy or ethical considerations prevent public deposition. Applicable to Basic and Share upon Request policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data subject to third party restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: "The data that support the findings of this study are available [from] [third party]. Restrictions apply to the availability of these data, which were used under license for this study. Data are available [from the authors / at URL] with the permission of [third party]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the third party and explain licensing/permission requirements and how data can be obtained (authors or third party). Useful when data cannot be shared freely because of third‑party licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data available on request from the authors (generic)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author, [author initials], upon reasonable request."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use where data are not publicly deposited but will be shared by authors upon reasonable request. Clarify who to contact and any conditions for requests. Marked for Basic and Share upon Request policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing not applicable – no new data generated
rubrics_metrics.description: "Data sharing is not applicable to this article as no new data were created or analyzed in this study."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for reviews, commentaries, or theoretical papers that did not create or analyze new data. Applicable across policies (All).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-digital data available
rubrics_metrics.description: "Non-digital data supporting this study are curated at [add location]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For physical/non-digital datasets (e.g., museum specimens, physical archives), give precise curation/location details so others can access or request access. Policy: All.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data not available due to [ethical/legal/commercial] restrictions (generic)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Due to the nature of the research, due to [ethical/legal/commercial] supporting data is not available."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the general reason for unavailability (ethical/legal/commercial). Be explicit about the restriction type so readers understand why data cannot be shared. Policy: All.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data not available – participant consent limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: "The participants of this study did not give written consent for their data to be shared publicly, so due to the sensitive nature of the research supporting data is not available."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify that lack of participant consent prevents public sharing. Explain sensitivity and, if possible, whether anonymized or aggregated versions could be shared or whether data can be requested under conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and heading of the data availability statement in the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Include your data availability statement within the text of your manuscript, before your ‘References’ section. Give it the heading ‘Data availability statement’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the DAS in the manuscript body (not only in submission forms) so it is openly visible on publication. Taylor & Francis makes DAS openly available on articles; this aids transparency and credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match statement to journal data policy (policy compatibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of these suggested statements can only be used when publishing in journals which have the basic or share upon reasonable request data policy. Check the ‘Policy’ column below to see which ones you can use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before selecting/adapting a template, verify the target journal’s data sharing policy (All, Basic, Share upon Request). Use templates consistent with that policy to avoid policy violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-anonymous peer review caution (anonymity risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are submitting to a journal where submissions are double-anonymous peer reviewed, then the main text file should not include any information that might identify the authors. As a data availability statement could reveal your identity, we recommend following the guide on data sharing in journals that offer double-anonymous peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing a DAS for double-anonymous review, avoid including identifiable information (e.g., dataset DOIs or repository entries that reveal authorship) in the manuscript; follow publisher guidance for anonymizing or delaying details until after review.
